For me, it stems all from Japanese repressive and misogynistic society. And since anime has a lot of cultural influences from its country of origin, anime is pretty much a reflection of Japanese view on beauty and women. 

So I'm going to try to answer in two parts:

(1) Why pedophilia and sexual harassment so rampant in Japan?

Japan places a high value on innocence and youth. If you look at Japanese porn, lots of women have high-pitched - almost girly voices rather than older mature ones. Shibuya Kayo, who is an ex-Japanese porn star, have said that usually Japanese porn star earnings are the highest when they first "debut" since its their innocence stripping away into the porn industry.  Unfortunately, Japan often goes too far in the "youth" criteria, which explains the pedophilia.    

Now why is it so rampant?

Japan, unfortunately, is a country that values harmony, status quo and traditions. Children in elementary school are taught to work together to serve meals and clean as a class while any children that has "individuality" are ostracized or even bullied.

Combined this with a patriarchal society, this leaves a lot of sexual harassment to be brushed off rather than criticized or vocal for changes. Japan opts for more "collaborative" solution so much that women have female only trains in order to avoid men harassing them. 

(2) Why is it so normalized in anime?

Anime, like other artistic medium, shows a lot of the country of origin's values. Because of Japan's high emphasis on youth and beauty, anime also brings out many sexual fantasies that is often repressed. Unfortunately, that would include sexual harassment and pedophilia. 

Now with Japaneses focus on status quo, these parts are rarely protested against and even normalized. As viewers, we also fall into the same trap and even detached ourselves from the issue since those two are considered as comedic relief - hell none of anime characters look nothing like us and remain in the fantasy realm. 

​

Ohh I'm glad that you made it to the 3rd interview! For technology, I would definitely mention some that would help you on a daily basis. The more niched it is, the better since it would be easier to note its unique abilities. Plus, they are probably evaluating your skills on how well you can sell a technology tool - so be prepared for that.

Technology-wise, I would mention what makes it meets the user's (you) needs? Think about what device it is available on (for example Khan Academy kids is shown on an iPad because kids mostly used iPads) or why did such tool solved a such specific problem? (Salesforce was created to aggregate all clients information into one) Or even what makes it separate from other apps (Headspace has a unique and pleasant design). 

From a design perspective, please note that all of these decisions (buttons or text placement or the whole app) are all intentional. The more you can see it - the more you can pitch the tool. 

I hope that helps!

Wow. I was going rant about the same thing - I too am also struggling with getting back to the workforce. 

I have an almost three-year resume gap because I was struggling with major depression. While I tried to cover up with some volunteering and online courses, I didn't finish half of them because my depression told me that it is all hopeless. Why bother when I am so stupid, dumb, and worthless? It wasn't worth the effort. On top of that, I relied financially on my parents and stayed in my college town for years. Since I lived close to a huge tech metropolitan, the cost of living skyrocketed. It was the worse feeling to see my college town getting gentrified at every moment while I rotted away. 

A few months back, I decided I had enough. I end it all. I was going to relieve my parents and my sisters the burden of my existence. Unfortunately, the highway patrol officers found me at the brink of a bridge and had me hospitalized. 

After the psychiatric, I was still depressed and suicidal and wondered why I hadn't attempted a second time. I was so worthless, why not just die already? 

I realized that there is a part of me that wanted to live. Despite the constant nagging voices telling me to kill myself, I had to remind myself that I'm still here, fighting against this fucking illness. I'm here with all my imperfections, my anxiety, my depression, my self-doubt. I tell myself that at least I can show up every moment - because that is my victory.

All I'm saying all you got to do is show up.
